entries.name: Apollo
entries.detail: Light, music, prophecy, and truth. Apollo came to be identified with the sun. The origin of his name is debated.

entries.name: Athena
entries.detail: Wisdom, strategic warfare, and crafts. A familiar account places her birth at the head of Zeus.

entries.name: Anubis
entries.detail: The guide of the dead attends the balance in the weighing of the heart. Ma’at supplies the standard of truth, and Osiris presides over judgment.

entries.name: Alpha
entries.detail: The first Greek letter, derived from the Phoenician letter aleph, whose name means ox.

entries.name: Ares
entries.detail: The god of war, associated with the tumult of combat.

entries.name: Atlas
entries.detail: The Titan who bears the heavens. His name is used for the uppermost cervical vertebra and for collections of maps.

entries.name: Avalon
entries.detail: In Geoffrey of Monmouth’s account, Arthur’s sword Caliburn was forged on Avalon, where the wounded Arthur was eventually taken.

entries.name: Brahma
entries.detail: The creator in the Trimurti alongside Vishnu and Shiva, associated with the Vedas and cosmic generation.

entries.name: Baldr
entries.detail: A radiant god, son of Odin and Frigg. His death precedes Ragnarök in the mythic sequence.

entries.name: Bastet
entries.detail: A protective goddess depicted in lioness and cat forms and associated with music and celebration.

entries.name: Beth / Bayit
entries.detail: Beth is the name of the second letter. Hebrew bayit is the word for house or dwelling.

entries.name: Brigid
entries.detail: Traditions link the goddess Brigid and namesakes to poetry, healing, and smithcraft.

entries.name: Boreas
entries.detail: The personified north wind, associated with cold and winter weather.

entries.name: Beowulf
entries.detail: The Geatish hero battles Grendel, Grendel’s mother, and a dragon.

entries.name: Chronos / Cronus
entries.detail: Chronos personifies time. Cronus is the Titan of the Golden Age. The names and figures overlap in some later traditions.

entries.name: Cerberus
entries.detail: The hound who guards the entrance to the Greek Underworld, often depicted with three heads.

entries.name: Circe
entries.detail: The sorceress of Aeaea transforms Odysseus’s crew, restores them, and gives Odysseus directions for his onward journey.

entries.name: Cernunnos
entries.detail: An antlered figure attested in Gaulish iconography. Broader associations with wild animals and natural cycles are interpretations.

entries.name: Chimera
entries.detail: A fire-breathing creature combining lion, goat, and serpent. In biology the term describes an organism with cell populations from genetically distinct sources.

entries.name: Camelot
entries.detail: The legendary location of Arthur’s court in medieval romance.

entries.name: Cosmos
entries.detail: Order, arrangement, or ornament. The word came to designate an ordered universe.

entries.name: Gaia
entries.detail: The personified Earth. In Hesiod she bears Uranus, the starry sky, and Pontus, the sea.

entries.name: Ganesha
entries.detail: The elephant-headed deity associated with wisdom, beginnings, and removing obstacles.

entries.name: Gabriel
entries.detail: A messenger in Daniel and Luke. The Hebrew name is built from the G-B-R family and El. See the Hebrew name notes.

entries.name: Gimel / Gamma
entries.detail: Greek gamma follows Phoenician gimel. Camel and throwing stick are proposed readings for the early sign.

entries.name: Gilgamesh
entries.detail: The king of Uruk seeks immortality after his companion Enkidu dies.

entries.name: Gorgon
entries.detail: The sisters Stheno, Euryale, and Medusa, associated with a petrifying gaze. Medusa was mortal.

entries.name: Grail
entries.detail: The vessel at the center of a quest in Arthurian romance. Its nature and significance vary by story.

entries.name: Hera
entries.detail: Queen of the Olympians and a goddess of marriage, associated with Zeus on Olympus.

entries.name: Hermes
entries.detail: Messenger, protector of travelers and boundaries, patron of commerce, and guide of the dead.

entries.name: Horus
entries.detail: A falcon deity associated with the sky and kingship. Some traditions link his eyes with the sun and moon.

entries.name: Hestia
entries.detail: Goddess of the hearth and its sacred fire. The Homeric Hymn links her with first and last libations at banquets.

entries.name: Heracles / Hercules
entries.detail: The hero famed for his strength and Twelve Labors. Hercules is the familiar Roman name.

entries.name: Hades
entries.detail: Ruler of the Underworld, where Persephone is queen. The name also came to refer to the realm.

entries.name: Het / Eta
entries.detail: Greek eta comes through Phoenician heth, whose early sign is often read as a fence or enclosure.

entries.name: Isis
entries.detail: A major goddess of magic, healing, and motherhood, associated with restoring Osiris and protecting Horus.

entries.name: Indra
entries.detail: A deity of storms and thunder who wields the vajra in the Vedic hymns.

entries.name: Iris
entries.detail: Personification of the rainbow and a messenger of the gods.

entries.name: Icarus
entries.detail: The son of Daedalus who falls after flying too close to the sun on wings fastened with wax.

entries.name: Ishtar / Inanna
entries.detail: Akkadian Ishtar and Sumerian Inanna are closely identified goddesses associated with love, war, and power.

entries.name: Izanagi & Izanami
entries.detail: The creator pair who stir the waters with a jeweled spear in accounts of the islands’ formation.

entries.name: Iota / Yod
entries.detail: Greek iota follows Phoenician yod, with an early sign associated with a hand or arm.

entries.name: Jupiter / Jove
entries.detail: Roman deity of the sky and thunder. Jupiter and Zeus belong to the inherited Indo-European sky-god name family.

entries.name: Janus
entries.detail: God of beginnings, doorways, and transitions, often depicted with two faces. January bears his name.

entries.name: Juno
entries.detail: Queen of the Roman gods, associated with marriage and civic protection. She is conventionally equated with Greek Hera.

entries.name: Jormungandr
entries.detail: The World Serpent encircling Midgard, who confronts Thor at Ragnarök. Also written Jörmungandr.

entries.name: Jade Emperor / Yu Huang
entries.detail: A celestial sovereign in Daoist and Chinese popular religion, frequently portrayed presiding over a divine bureaucracy.

entries.name: Jotun
entries.detail: A member of the jötnar, beings who appear in kinship and conflict with Norse gods.

entries.name: J
entries.detail: Developed as a written variant of I. Its use as a separate consonant letter became established gradually.

entries.name: Kali
entries.detail: A fierce goddess associated with time, transformation, and destruction. Her roles vary across devotional traditions.

entries.name: Krishna
entries.detail: A major deity, often identified as an avatar of Vishnu, who teaches Arjuna in the Bhagavad Gita.

entries.name: Kronos
entries.detail: Another romanization of Cronus, the Titan overthrown by Zeus. Compare Chronos / Cronus under C.

entries.name: Kaph / Kappa
entries.detail: Greek kappa follows Phoenician kaph, a letter name associated with the palm of a hand.

entries.name: Kitsune
entries.detail: The Japanese word for fox. Fox spirits in folklore are often depicted with shapeshifting abilities and sometimes multiple tails.

entries.name: Khonsu
entries.detail: A lunar deity whose name is often interpreted in connection with traveling.

entries.name: Kukulkan
entries.detail: A Maya feathered serpent figure especially associated with Yucatán. Compare Quetzalcoatl under Q.

entries.name: Loki
entries.detail: The shapeshifting trickster who helps and harms the gods in different stories. The association with fire is an interpretation.

entries.name: Lakshmi
entries.detail: Goddess of prosperity, fortune, beauty, and abundance.

entries.name: Lugh
entries.detail: Known for mastery of many arts and associated with the festival Lughnasadh. His name’s relation to light is debated.

entries.name: Lamed / Lambda
entries.detail: Greek lambda comes through Phoenician lamed. An ox goad is the usual interpretation of the early sign.

entries.name: Logos
entries.detail: A word with senses including word, speech, account, or reason. Its philosophical and scriptural meanings depend on the passage.

entries.name: Leto
entries.detail: The Titaness who bears Apollo and Artemis.

entries.name: Leviathan
entries.detail: A sea creature described in Job 41 and elsewhere in the KJV, with comparisons to other ancient Near Eastern sea-monster traditions.

entries.name: Mercury
entries.detail: God of trade and a messenger. His name is commonly linked to the Latin family for merchandise or commerce.

entries.name: Minerva
entries.detail: Goddess of crafts, intellect, and strategy, commonly compared to Athena. The name’s deeper derivation is debated.

entries.name: Morpheus
entries.detail: In Ovid, a maker of dream figures who imitates human forms. Greek morphē means form or shape.

entries.name: Mem / Mu
entries.detail: Greek mu follows Phoenician mem, whose early sign is conventionally associated with water.

entries.name: Ma'at
entries.detail: Truth, justice, and right order, also personified as a goddess. Compare the heart-weighing scene under Anubis.

entries.name: Mars
entries.detail: God of war and a protector invoked in agricultural rites. The origin of the name is uncertain.

entries.name: Maya
entries.detail: Māyā has senses such as art, power, or illusion in different texts. The proposed measure association belongs to the source interpretation.

entries.name: Nyx
entries.detail: The primordial personification of night.

entries.name: Nike
entries.detail: The winged personification of victory. The Greek noun means victory.

entries.name: Neptune
entries.detail: God of waters, later closely identified with Poseidon. Moisture-related name roots are proposed.

entries.name: Nun / Nu
entries.detail: Greek nu follows Phoenician nun. Fish is a traditional interpretation of the letter name, with other proposals for the early sign.

entries.name: Nemesis
entries.detail: A personification of retribution or due allotment. Her name is associated with the Greek family for distributing or apportioning.

entries.name: Nergal
entries.detail: A deity associated with war, disease, and the Underworld. Scorching heat is one association.

entries.name: Nirvana
entries.detail: Literally associated with extinguishing or blowing out. In Buddhist contexts the term concerns liberation and the cessation of suffering.

entries.name: Odin
entries.detail: One-eyed seeker of knowledge and runes. His name family is associated with inspiration, excitement, or frenzy.

entries.name: Osiris
entries.detail: God of the dead and regeneration, associated with agriculture and continuity after death. His name’s derivation is uncertain.

entries.name: Orion
entries.detail: The giant hunter placed among the stars in Greek myth. The constellation has long served as a seasonal marker.

entries.name: Ayin / Omicron
entries.detail: Phoenician ayin, associated with an eye, supplied the ancestral sign for Greek omicron.

entries.name: Ouroboros
entries.detail: A serpent eating its own tail. The Greek term names the tail-devouring image.

entries.name: Oceanus
entries.detail: The Titan and world-encircling river in archaic Greek cosmology.

entries.name: Oracle
entries.detail: A prophetic answer, the medium that delivers one, or the place of consultation. The Latin word family includes speaking or praying.

entries.name: Poseidon
entries.detail: God of the sea, earthquakes, and horses. Interpretations of his name as lord or husband of earth are proposals.

entries.name: Persephone
entries.detail: Queen of the Underworld. Her return from below ground is linked to seasonal fertility. The supplied name roots are conjectural.

entries.name: Prometheus
entries.detail: The Titan who brings fire to humanity. His name is traditionally understood as forethought.

entries.name: Pe / Pi
entries.detail: Greek pi follows Phoenician pe, whose name is associated with the mouth.

entries.name: Pan
entries.detail: A deity of shepherds, flocks, and wild places, and the namesake of panic. His proposed name derivation is uncertain.

entries.name: Pneuma
entries.detail: Wind, breath, or spirit depending on context.

entries.name: Pluto
entries.detail: A name for the ruler of the Underworld, associated with wealth and resources from beneath the ground.

entries.name: Quetzalcoatl
entries.detail: The Nahuatl name combines quetzal plumage with serpent. This feathered serpent is associated with wind and creation in several traditions.

entries.name: Quirinus
entries.detail: An early Roman deity later associated with the deified Romulus. Proposed name explanations include a civic assembly and a spear.

entries.name: Quintessence
entries.detail: Fifth essence. In ancient and medieval natural philosophy it names the fifth element distinct from earth, water, air, and fire.

entries.name: Qoph / Koppa
entries.detail: Greek koppa follows Phoenician qoph. Head and needle-eye readings are among the proposals for the early sign.

entries.name: Quantum
entries.detail: Latin quantum asks how much. Modern physics uses quantum for a discrete quantity in a particular system.

entries.name: Quake
entries.detail: To shake or tremble, from Old English cwacian.

entries.name: Quest
entries.detail: A search or pursuit. The word traces through French to the Latin family of quaerere, to seek.

entries.name: Ra
entries.detail: A solar deity whose name is the Egyptian word for sun.

entries.name: Rhea
entries.detail: The Titaness and mother of a generation of Olympians. Flow and earth are proposed readings of her name.

entries.name: Rta
entries.detail: Ṛta concerns right order in Vedic texts, encompassing ritual and cosmic regularity.

entries.name: Resh / Rho
entries.detail: Greek rho follows Phoenician resh, whose early sign is associated with the head.

entries.name: Ruach
entries.detail: Wind, breath, or spirit. The sense depends on context.

entries.name: Romulus
entries.detail: The legendary founder of Rome and brother of Remus. Historical explanations of the name are uncertain.

entries.name: Runes
entries.detail: Characters of several early Germanic alphabets. The word family is associated with a secret or counsel.

entries.name: Sol
entries.detail: The Latin word for sun, also personified as a Roman deity.

entries.name: Set / Seth
entries.detail: A deity associated with deserts, storms, and conflict. The origin and interpretation of the name are debated.

entries.name: Saturn
entries.detail: A deity associated with agriculture and a legendary Golden Age. Ancient writers connected the name with sowing.

entries.name: Shin / Sigma
entries.detail: Greek sigma is historically linked to the Semitic letter shin, whose name is associated with tooth.

entries.name: Shiva
entries.detail: A major deity whose name is commonly glossed auspicious. Traditions connect him with dissolution and renewal.

entries.name: Sophia
entries.detail: Wisdom, skill, or expertise, depending on the source and context.

entries.name: Sovereign
entries.detail: A ruler or holder of supreme authority. The word family traces to a form meaning above.

entries.name: Theseus
entries.detail: The legendary Athenian king and labyrinth traveler. Nathan Tabor’s sound reading is “the Zeus.”

entries.name: Theos
entries.detail: A Greek word rendered as God or god by context. John 10:34–35 quotes Psalm 82:6 and uses plural forms for “gods.” Nathan Tabor’s sound reading is “the OS.”

entries.name: Thanos
entries.detail: Marvel’s Titan uses the Infinity Stones to erase half the population. Nathan Tabor’s sound reading is “thank NOS - nitrous oxide.”

entries.name: Taw
entries.detail: A historical ancestor of Greek tau and Latin T. The Hebrew word taw means a mark in Ezekiel 9:4 (KJV).

entries.name: Tiwaz / Tyr / Tiw
entries.detail: A name family associated with the Germanic deity Týr and oaths. “The Was” is the sound reading explored in the source notes.

entries.name: Thoth / Tehuti
entries.detail: A deity of writing, reckoning, and learned arts. “Thought” is the sound reading explored in the source notes.

entries.name: Tengri
entries.detail: A term associated with heaven, the sky, and the deity in steppe traditions.

entries.name: Tonatiuh
entries.detail: A solar figure associated with the Fifth Sun.

entries.name: Tlaloc
entries.detail: A deity of rain, storms, and fertility.

entries.name: Tiamat
entries.detail: The primordial sea in Enūma Eliš. Marduk divides her body to form the cosmos.

entries.name: Tao
entries.detail: The Way or path, romanized Tao or Dao.

entries.name: Tesla
entries.detail: The SI unit of magnetic flux density, named for Nikola Tesla.

entries.name: Torque
entries.detail: The moment of a force about a point or axis.

entries.name: Thor
entries.detail: The thunder figure cross-referenced from B.

entries.name: Taw / Tau
entries.detail: A crossed mark is an early form associated with the letter that became Greek tau.

entries.name: Titan
entries.detail: A member of the divine generation preceding the Olympians. The proposed sun and stretch roots are uncertain.

entries.name: Tithēmi
entries.detail: To place, put, or establish.

entries.name: Uranus
entries.detail: Ouranos is the personified sky, born from Gaia in Hesiod.

entries.name: Utu
entries.detail: A sun deity linked with seeing, legal judgment, and justice. Compare Akkadian Shamash.

entries.name: Ushas
entries.detail: Uṣas, the dawn, is both a natural phenomenon and a deity in the Vedic hymns.

entries.name: Upsilon
entries.detail: A letter historically derived from Phoenician waw. Compare Vav / Waw under V.

entries.name: Uraeus
entries.detail: The erect cobra emblem associated with kingship and protection.

entries.name: Umbra
entries.detail: Shadow or shade.

entries.name: Ullr
entries.detail: A deity associated with archery and travel on skis. The linkage to a Germanic word for glory is a proposal.

entries.name: Verbum
entries.detail: Word. The Latin Vulgate uses Verbum for Logos in John 1:1.

entries.name: Veritas
entries.detail: Truth or truthfulness.

entries.name: Vita
entries.detail: Life.

entries.name: Vox
entries.detail: Voice, utterance, or sound.

entries.name: Varuna
entries.detail: A deity connected with moral and cosmic order.

entries.name: Vayu
entries.detail: Wind and the deity of wind.

entries.name: Vav / Waw
entries.detail: A letter name associated with a hook. The prefixed letter can express “and.” Its numeric value is six.

entries.name: Vulcan
entries.detail: The Roman deity associated with fire and the forge.

entries.name: Vector
entries.detail: A quantity represented by magnitude and direction in elementary geometry and physics.

entries.name: Volt
entries.detail: The SI unit of electric potential difference, named after Alessandro Volta.

entries.name: Woden
entries.detail: The Old English cognate of Odin. Interpretations of the name include inspiration, frenzy, or fury.

entries.name: Wyrd
entries.detail: Fate or what comes to pass, associated with the verb weorþan, to become.

entries.name: Wakan
entries.detail: Wakȟáŋ conveys sacredness or mystery. Its cultural and spiritual meanings depend on use and context.

entries.name: W
entries.detail: Developed from doubled U or V letter forms to represent a sound needed in Germanic writing.

entries.name: Way
entries.detail: A path, route, or manner of going, from Old English weg.

entries.name: Will
entries.detail: Desire, volition, or intention, from a family including Old English willa.

entries.name: Xolotl
entries.detail: Xōlōtl is associated with twinship, movement through the Underworld, and guiding the sun in some accounts.

entries.name: Xenia
entries.detail: Guest-friendship and reciprocal hospitality between host and visitor.

entries.name: Xi / Chi
entries.detail: Xi is historically linked with Semitic samekh. Chi is a separate Greek letter whose remote origin is debated.

entries.name: Xiphos
entries.detail: Sword. The name also identifies a type of ancient Greek double-edged sword.

entries.name: Xeros
entries.detail: Dry. The combining form appears in words such as xeric and xerography.

entries.name: X
entries.detail: Used as an unknown in algebra and as a crossing mark in different graphic contexts.

entries.name: Ymir
entries.detail: The primordial being whose body supplies material for the world in Norse accounts. Twin is a proposed name interpretation.

entries.name: Yama
entries.detail: A figure linked with the first mortals and the realm of the dead. His name is commonly linked with twin.

entries.name: Yod
entries.detail: A letter associated with a hand or arm in historical alphabet charts. Compare Iota / Yod under I.

entries.name: Yin & Yang
entries.detail: Terms with early associations to shaded and sunny sides of a hill and a broader range of paired cosmological uses.

entries.name: Yggdrasil
entries.detail: The world tree. Its name is traditionally interpreted as the horse of Yggr, a name of Odin.

entries.name: Yoke
entries.detail: A crosspiece joining a pair of draft animals. It belongs to an Indo-European word family for joining.

entries.name: Zeus
entries.detail: The sky and thunder god, whose name belongs to the inherited Indo-European sky-god family.

entries.name: Zephyrus
entries.detail: The personified west wind, associated with spring in some accounts.

entries.name: Zoe
entries.detail: Zōē means life. The word belongs to the broad Indo-European family for living.

entries.name: Zayin / Zeta
entries.detail: Greek zeta follows Phoenician zayin. Weapon is a traditional interpretation of the Semitic name.

entries.name: Zenith
entries.detail: The point directly overhead. The word traces to Arabic samt al-raʾs, direction of the head.

entries.name: Zero
entries.detail: From Arabic ṣifr, empty. Zero functions as a number and as a positional placeholder.
